readerQuestion: How can Home Assistant give me one daily list of low sensor batteries without including every phone or silently treating missing readings as healthy?
directAnswer: Label the battery entities to monitor and run one daily time-triggered check. Include valid percentages at or below the selected limit and binary battery-low indicators; put unknown, unavailable or unsupported readings in a separate check list. Update one persistent Home Assistant notification and dismiss it when the next check is clear. Validate the selected entities and list before adding phone push. Reported levels do not prove a sensor still works, and the daily trigger does not catch up after downtime.
originalContribution: Sections 1–4 and the complete YAML under #configuration combine directly labeled scope, percentage and binary indicators, empty-selection warnings, finite numeric range validation, separate missing-reading messages, and create/dismiss behavior. The worked table under #worked-example follows 20%, 0%, a binary low flag, an unavailable sensor, a normal sensor and an excluded phone across daily checks. The troubleshooting table explains wrong labels, unsupported types, duplicate readings and stale values. The published YAML and template passed 22 automated simulated cases, including boundary values and clearing only the owned notification.
limitations: Documentation research and simulated Jinja2/PyYAML checks only. No running Home Assistant installation, physical battery, device longevity, scheduler delivery or phone-delivery test was performed. The 20% threshold is illustrative, not universal manufacturer advice. The configuration cannot detect a stale but syntactically valid percentage or recover a missed scheduled run. Phone push and source integrations may depend on cloud services. Actual publishing, deployment and search indexing are not assessed by these local checks.

claimChecks.claim: The battery sensor device class represents remaining charge as a percentage.
For a battery binary sensor, on means low and off means normal; battery_charging is a different class.
label_entities returns directly labeled entities and does not inherit labels applied to a device or area.
A numeric-state trigger reacts to crossing a threshold and does not repeatedly fire while the state stays on that side.
Reusing notification_id with persistent_notification.create overwrites the existing notification.
persistent_notification.dismiss removes the notification specified by notification_id.
is_number checks finite numeric convertibility and rejects unavailable, unknown, infinity and NaN before comparison.
Companion notifications use the phone-specific notify.mobile_app action and require a message; persistent notification clearing is separate.
Ordinary phone notification delivery can involve external push services.
